To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

peroxisome-proliferator feeding causes a transient down-regulation of several hepatocyte plasma membrane protein domains that are expressed in the proliferative period following partial hepatectomy, and that the feeding of peroxisome profilers causes the induction of a more basic isoform of the hepatocyte basolateral plasma protein CE 9, which is not induced by partial hepatectom

the peroxisomal proliferator-induced alterations of the expression and modification (i.e., the posttranslatory processing) of the rat hepatocytic plasma membrane proteins were specific to the peroxisomally active compounds, occurred early in the pleiotropic peroxisome-proliferator response, were reversible upon the removal of the compound, and were similar to the changes that occur in hepatocytes during the period of proliferation following two-thirds partial hepatectomy.

the peroxisomal proliferator-induced pleiotropic response in rat liver is characterized, in part, by changes in the expression and posttranslational modifications of the rat hepatocytes surface membrane proteins, and that the changes in the expression, modification and localization of the basolaterally expressed CE 9 protein are a specific marker of the hepatocellular response to peroxisomal proliferation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the perox-isome proliferators on the expression and posttranslational modifications of the hepatocyte membrane proteins.

the hypothesis that the pleiotropic effects of peroxisome profilers on the hepatocyte are mediated, at least in part, by the down-regulation and modification of the expression of specific plasma membrane proteins and that these alterations are involved in the hepatocarcinogenic response of the liver to peroxisomal proliferation.

the effects of peroxisome-proliferator-induced pleiotropic changes in hepatocyte differentiation on the expression, posttranslational modifications, and localization of the rat hepatocytes' plasma membrane proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

peroxisome profilers cause a pleiotropic response in the hepatocyte that is manifested by a number of alterations in the expression, modification and/or localization of the hepatocyte's plasma membrane proteins.

ciprofibrate and other peroxisone proliferators cause changes in the expression and post-translational modification of several rat hepatocyte plasma-membrane proteins, and these changes are reversible upon removal of the peroxiome proliferators from the diet.

the peroxisomal proliferators ciprofibrate, di(2ethylhexyl) phthalate, clofiibrate, and Wy 14,643 are capable of causing the selective downregulation of the epidermoid growth factor receptor, asialo-glycoprotein receptor and the integral plasma membrane proteins HA 321 and HA 4, while inducing a lower-Mr iso-form of the basolatera1 plasma membrane protein CE-9.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pleiotropic effects of peroxisome-proliferating chemicals on hepatocyte plasma membrane protein expression and modification may be useful in the development of new assays for the identification of peroxisomal proliferators and for the elucidation of the mechanisms of peroxisomc proliferation.

the pleiotropic effects of peroxisome-proliferating compounds on the liver are not limited to the induction of peroxisomal enzymes and peroxisome biogenesis but also include alterations in the expression, posttranslational processing, and/or localization of several plasma membrane proteins.

peroxisome prolifeators are able to induce the expression of a lower-Mr isoforms of the basolatera protein CE 9 in rat hepatocyte plasma membranes and to down-regulate the expression of the hepatocyte surface receptors for epidermal growth factors, asialoglycoproteins, and HA 321 and HA 4, as well as the plasma membrane enzyme dipeptidlypeptidase-IV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
peroxisome-proliferating compounds cause a number of pleiotropic effects on hepatocyte plasma membrane protein expression and modification.

ciprofibrate and related peroxisome-proliferating drugs cause the down-regulation in rat liver of the epidermoid growth factor receptor, dipeptidase, asialoglycoproteins receptor, and two other membrane proteins and the up-regulation of a basolateral protein, CE 9.

ciprofibrate causes the selective down-regulations of the hepatocyte surface receptors for epidermal growth factors and asialoglycoproteins, as well as two integral plasma membrane proteins (HA 321 and HA 4) that are associated with the hepatocyte plasma membranes.
